title: Verifying Declared AI Workloads from GPU Supply Current
abstract: arXiv:2611.29982v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Frontier AI governance agreements require compute verification techniques that allow an external observer to confirm that a hardware operator does not run prohibited workloads. Off-chip, analogue hardware signals, such as power draw, have been proposed as a potential information channel for compute verification. Such signals can be measured externally, without the operator's cooperation. We show that the supply current drawn by a GPU can be used to verify the work declared by the GPU operator, without requiring examples of prohibited workloads or evasion strategies. We record 23.4 h of GPU current with a Rogowski coil under idle, training and inference workloads. We consider five evasion strategies an operator might use to disguise prohibited training. translated_title: 基于GPU供电电流验证申报的AI工作负载
translated_abstract: 前沿AI治理协议需要计算验证技术，使外部观察者能够确认硬件运营商没有运行被禁止的工作负载。片外模拟硬件信号（如功耗）已被提出作为计算验证的潜在信息通道，这类信号可以在外部测量，无需运营商配合。我们证明，GPU汲取的供电电流可用于验证GPU运营商所申报的工作，而无需被禁止工作负载的示例或规避策略。我们使用罗氏线圈在空闲、训练和推理工作负载下记录了23.4小时的GPU电流，并考虑了运营商可能用来掩盖被禁止训练的五种规避策略。结果表明，仅用允许的、申报的工作（空闲和推理）的电流数据拟合的单类模型，能够标记出至少99.9%的被禁止训练时间窗口，包括被隐藏的训练。
tldr: 本研究提出利用外部可测量的GPU供电电流，通过仅基于正常申报工作负载训练的单类模型，即可检测出至少99.9%的被禁止训练窗口，为AI治理协议提供了一种无需运营商配合的计算验证方法。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that a one-class model trained only on declared, permitted GPU workloads can use externally measured supply current to flag at least 99.9% of prohibited training windows, enabling compute verification without operator cooperation or examples of forbidden workloads.
